subject: Request: provisional SLA exception for model v12.4 tail-latency regression
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@crystalbank.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: crystalbank-sre@crystalbank.com
Date: 2026-04-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p95 tail-latency regression on model v12.4 after 04/17 deploy

Hi Avery / Karthik,

Quick summary: after the v12.4 push yesterday evening our internal SREs are seeing a persistent p95 tail-latency increase for the inference endpoint serving model v12.4 (user-facing payments flow). Baseline p95 was ~210ms; since ~22:30 UTC on 2026-04-17 it's sustained ~420–520ms for a subset of traffic. This is impacting authorization throughput during peak windows.

Attached is a short trace export and a CSV of p95 by shard: p95_runbook.csv, sre-trace-20260417.log. We need urgent guidance on whether Redwood can provide: 1) provisional SLA carveout for the degradation window while we stabilize, or 2) an expedited rollback to v12.3 and associated authorization to proceed.

Our timeline: business-critical peak starts 2026-04-18 14:00 UTC. We need an operational decision within 6 hours.

Can you confirm the quickest safe path (pin traffic, temporary rate cap, rollback)? If rollback is needed, please call out an explicit rollback trigger (metric + duration) we can accept.

Thanks,
Sara Liu
Head of SRE, CrystalBank

Attachments: p95_runbook.csv (csv), sre-trace-20260417.log (text)

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@crystalbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 tail-latency regression on model v12.4 after 04/17 deploy

Sara — thanks for the quick heads up and for the artifacts. I'm looping in Monica (account lead) and Neha (support lead) to coordinate approvals and customer communication.

High-level response: we can support a provisional SLA exception for an agreed, timeboxed window while we run mitigations, OR we can authorize a controlled rollback to v12.3. We need to document the rollback trigger(s) and the canary plan before taking action.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Karthik: can you review the attached trace and propose rollback trigger thresholds (p95 absolute and duration) + a rollback playbook link we can reference?
- CrystalBank: confirm whether a 10% traffic cap to the endpoint during the next 2 hours is acceptable as an intermediate mitigation.

If CrystalBank prefers rollback, we'll need a signed operational exception (DocuSign) acknowledging temporary SLA adjustments for the rollback window — Monica, can you start that DocuSign? I've added a DocuSign link placeholder in related_links.

I'll stand by on call if you want to triage live.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

(Note: forwarding the trace to Karthik for immediate triage)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 tail-latency regression on model v12.4 after 04/17 deploy

Avery / Monica — quick technical assessment after a cursory look at sre-trace-20260417.log and the p95 CSV:

Observations:
- Latency appears concentrated on a subset of larger-context requests (seq len > 512) and on a small fraction of GPU workers where KV cache miss rates spiked post-deploy.
- Resource saturation is not global; rolling back those workers or draining hot shards should reduce p95 rapidly.

Proposed immediate playbook (summary):
1) Temporary mitigation (0–30m): apply a 10% traffic cap to highest-latency route + enable aggressive KV-prefix caching for that customer route (configurable).
2) If p95 remains > 350ms for > 15 minutes after mitigation -> trigger canary rollback to v12.3 on 10% of traffic.
3) If canary rollback reduces p95 below 250ms within 10 minutes -> escalate to full rollback authorization (operator sign-off required).
4) If rollback required, follow rollback_playbook.md (attached) for sequence, version pinning and cache warm-up steps.

Rollbacks have risk (higher token costs + potential for transient correctness differences). Recommendation: pursue mitigation + canary revert first; full rollback only if canary demonstrates benefit.

I'll stand by for an immediate runbook handoff. If we get authorization to canary, I can run the steps with Neha.

-Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback_playbook.md (markdown)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@crystalbank.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-19T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 tail-latency regression on model v12.4 after 04/17 deploy

Sara — thanks for the patience while we triaged. CrystalBank: Redwood can provisionally approve a timeboxed SLA exception for the impacted window under the following conditions:

1) Exception window: 2026-04-18 14:00 UTC to 2026-04-20 14:00 UTC (48 hours).
2) Mitigations you must accept now: 10% traffic cap on the affected route and KV-prefix caching enabled (per Karthik's guidance).
3) Rollback triggers: if p95 remains > 350ms for a continuous 15-minute window after mitigation, Redwood will initiate a canary rollback to v12.3 on 10% of traffic. If the canary reduces p95 to < 250ms within 10 minutes, Redwood will proceed to full rollback pending your confirmation.
4) Business acceptance: CrystalBank must sign a short operational exception acknowledging temporary SLA adjustment and cost/throughput implications. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/link/abc123

We will also open INF-7453 in Jira to track the mitigation work and a post-mortem. Action items for CrystalBank: confirm acceptance of the mitigation steps and sign the DocuSign by 2026-04-18 12:30 UTC. If you cannot sign in time and the window approaches, we will default to mitigation-only (no rollback) and continue monitoring.

Please reply with explicit "ACCEPT" or "DECLINE" and we will execute.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
